title: Node heartbeat latch and Terraform auto-repair playbook
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Background: Private VPC nodes occasionally enter a state where the node agent heartbeat latches (heartbeat visible but downstream probes fail intermittently) combined with small Terraform drift (metadata tags / subnet assignments). This ticket captures a pragmatic runbook and an idempotent automation flow to detect, safely repair, and validate these classes of failures without broad service disruption.

Goals: 1) Provide a deterministic detection heuristic for 'heartbeat-latch' vs full node failure. 2) Define safe, reversible terraform-based repair that can be run by automation or on-call. 3) Add guardrails (canary, dry-run, approvals) to reduce blast radius. 4) Add post-repair validation checks and observability hooks.

Scope: Applies to Redwood Private nodes (VPC) running inference runtime + agent daemons. Covers cases: agent heartbeat present but health checks fail (probe misrouting, SG/NACL drift, kernel incompat mismatch), resource metadata drift, and KV cache warm failures. Out-of-scope: complete disk corruption, BIOS-level failures, and customer-managed hardware repairs.
runbook_steps: 1) Triage: correlate alerts - alert type, node_id, last_successful_probe_ts, agent-heartbeat_ts, and terraform-state last apply. Use /console/incidents and node-trace logs.
2) Quick isolation - mark node as 'drain-candidate' in routing but do NOT immediately terminate. Run: curl -sS https://private-controlplane.local/nodes/{{node_id}}/status to capture payload.
3) Distinguish 'latched' vs 'down' - criteria: agent_heartbeat_age < 30s AND health_probe_failure_rate > 30% => latch case. If heartbeat_age > 120s treat as down and follow full-replacement flow.

4) Inspect network path: run traceroute/tcpdump from controlplane to node management IP; check security group rules against expected tags. Command examples: ssh ops@bastion -- sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 port 8080 -c 200; aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters Name=tag:Node,Values={{node_id}}.

5) Terraform dry-run to detect drift: cd infra/private && terraform init -backend-config=... && terraform plan -var node_id={{node_id}} -out=plan.tfplan. Save plan for audit. If plan contains only metadata/tag changes or SG/NACL updates consider safe to apply.

6) Safe apply workflow: (a) create a canary change by applying plan with target resource = node metadata and guard apply window 5 minutes, (b) after apply, run validation tests (see postmortem_checks), (c) if validation passes mark node as healthy and exit. Use: terraform apply -auto-approve plan.tfplan --target=module.node["{{node_id}}"].metadata

7) KV-cache warm and runtime validation: after network/metadata repair, trigger cache warm: curl -X POST https://node-{{node_id}}.local/internal/warm_kv -H 'Authorization: Bearer <ops-token>' and validate stats via /metrics (kv_cache_hit_ratio > 0.6 sustained).

8) Rollforward vs restart policy: prefer non-disruptive rollforward. If latching persists after repairs, trigger a rolling agent restart: ssh ops@node && sudo systemctl restart redwood-agent && monitor for 2x probe cycles. If still failing, schedule node replacement (controlled drain -> terminate -> terraform apply to recreate).
9) Observability hooks: attach run_id to traces and create temporary per-node dashboard with 1h retention. Add annotation to incident: GitHub PR or Confluence link and terraform plan file path.
10) Post-incident: open a postmortem if more than 2 nodes affected or customer impact > medium; include metrics, timeline, and automation improvement actions.
Safety notes: All terraform applies MUST be logged, use plan files saved to s3://infra-ops/plans/{{run_id}}; automation must require a signed-off policy for changes that touch security groups or IAM.
automation_playbooks: playbook/heartbeat-latch-detector: lambda that consumes node-health-stream, applies heuristic (heartbeat_age, probe_error_rate) and writes candidate to SQS with severity tag.
playbook/terraform-diff-checker: orchestrates terraform init/plan in a sandbox, validates plan contains only allowed resource types (tags, SG peer updates) and produces a safety score.
playbook/auto-apply-with-canary: runs terraform apply with --target and creates a canary validation job (5 minutes) that executes the runbook tests and auto-rolls back on failure.
playbook/kv-warm-and-validate: posts warm request, collects kv cache metrics, and publishes result to monitoring channel.

playbook/replace-node-ami-rollback: if rolling restart fails twice, triggers controlled drain, terraform destroy for node resource, then terraform apply to recreate; post-create validation run follows.
postmortem_checks: metrics to capture: probe_failure_rate (1m/5m), agent_heartbeat_age, tcp_retransmits, kv_cache_hit_ratio, cpu_steal, network_errors
validate: terraform plan diff (JSON) stored in s3 and attached to incident
check kernel/driver mismatches: compare /proc/version and installed inference runtime version against fleet baseline
correlate with upstream infra events (cloud provider maintenance, ASG scale events) and with recent CI/CD deployments in the same subnet
if repeated across multiple AZs, escalate to infra reliability and consider circuit-breaker tuning for autoscaler
rollback_plan: If canary apply fails: run terraform apply -destroy -target=<changed-resource> is NOT allowed; instead apply the inverse plan previously saved (s3://infra-ops/plans/{{run_id}}/rollback-plan.tfplan)
If agent restart causes regressions: revert to previous agent config via consul kv rollback key redwood/agent/config/{{node_id}} and restart
If terraform recreation is required and validation fails post-create: isolate node and attach to a degraded pool for manual debugging; do not reintroduce to prod until green-validation passes

2026-02-25 | Priya Nair: Reviewed the canary validation checks. Suggested adding kv_cache_hit_ratio threshold and an automated warm step. Priya approved moving to automation prototype.

2026-03-03 | Security Bot: Reminder - any automation that modifies security groups must include an audit trail and require two approvers for production applies. Marked security_review_required=false but SOC should be notified when SG changes are in plan.

2026-03-10 | Marco Diaz: Automation prototype merged to staging branch: playbook/heartbeat-latch-detector. Running manual canary applies for three nodes this week. Observability hooks added to incident pipeline.
